```{r}
#| include: false
source("0_set_up.R")
source("R/codebook.R")        # dataset_citation()
source("R/page_helpers.R")    # aa_stats_html()
update_derived_data()         # copies from the research drive; skipped in CI

k12_ev  <- read.csv("data/derived/k12_door_security_events_v2025.csv")
k12_dr  <- read.csv("data/derived/k12_door_security_doors_v2025.csv")
ofc     <- read.csv("data/derived/officer_shot_data_v2025.csv",
                    colClasses = c(officer_id = "character"))
ofc_yr  <- as.integer(substr(ofc$date, 1, 4))

yr_span <- function(y) paste0(min(y, na.rm = TRUE), "–", max(y, na.rm = TRUE))
posted  <- "2026"   # year both datasets went up on the site (citation year)

k12_cit <- dataset_citation("K-12 Door Security Dataset", "alerrt_k12_door_security", "2025", posted,
                            "https://activeattackdata.org/datasets.html#k-12-door-security")
ofc_cit <- dataset_citation("Officers Shot in Active Shooter Incidents", "alerrt_officers_shot", "2025", posted,
                            "https://activeattackdata.org/datasets.html#officers-shot")

bibtex_block <- function(cit) {
  cat("<details class=\"cb-bibtex\"><summary>BibTeX</summary>\n\n```bibtex\n", cit$bibtex,
      "\n```\n\n</details>\n", sep = "")
}
```

::: {.aa-intro}
# More data

Two datasets built from the Active Attack Data: the doors attackers met in K-12 school attacks, and the officers shot in active shooter incidents.

Each comes as CSV files with a PDF codebook, in the same form as the [Active Attack Data](1_visuals.html#download-the-data). Jump to [K-12 door security](#k-12-door-security) or [Officers shot](#officers-shot).
:::

## K-12 door security {#k-12-door-security .cb-h2}

U.S. K-12 active shooter attacks and the doors the attackers came up against: whether each door was locked, barricaded or breached, and how the attacker got through.

::: {.cb-facts}
```{r}
#| echo: false
knitr::asis_output(aa_stats_html(c("Attacks" = nrow(k12_ev), "Doors" = nrow(k12_dr),
                                   "Years" = yr_span(k12_ev$year), "Version" = "2025")))
```

::: {.aa-downloads .cb-downloads}
{{< downloadthis data/derived/k12_door_security_events_v2025.csv dname="k12_door_security_events_v2025" label="Events (CSV)" >}}
{{< downloadthis data/derived/k12_door_security_doors_v2025.csv dname="k12_door_security_doors_v2025" label="Doors (CSV)" >}}
{{< downloadthis data/derived/k12_door_security_codebook_v2025.pdf dname="k12_door_security_codebook_v2025" label="Codebook (PDF)" >}}
:::
:::

::: {.cb-reading}
::: {.cb-reason}
### Two files
The events file has one row per attack (`{r} nrow(k12_ev)` rows, `{r} ncol(k12_ev)` variables): school, timing, victims by location, attackers, firearms and the response. The doors file has one row per door (`{r} nrow(k12_dr)` doors in `{r} length(unique(k12_dr$case_number))` attacks, `{r} ncol(k12_dr)` variables).
:::
::: {.cb-reason}
### Linking them
The files share one column, `case_number`. To look at doors by an event characteristic, such as school level, join the events file to the doors file on `case_number`.
:::
::: {.cb-reason}
### Doors
Each door is recorded as coded and grouped as in the 2026 report: lock type, status (locked, unlocked, propped), breach attempts, barricades, whether the attacker got through, and by what route.
:::
::: {.cb-reason}
### Funding and report
Collection of the `{r} yr_span(k12_ev$year)` data was funded by the Security Industry Association and first reported in ALERRT's *The Role of Locked Doors and Access Control in School-Based Active Shooter Events* (2026). Where this version differs from the report, this version is the corrected one.
:::
:::

## Officers shot {#officers-shot .cb-h2}

Law enforcement officers struck by gunfire during active shooter incidents: where they were, how they were hit, and what they were doing at the time.

::: {.cb-facts}
```{r}
#| echo: false
knitr::asis_output(aa_stats_html(c("Officers" = nrow(ofc), "Incidents" = length(unique(ofc$case_id)),
                                   "Killed" = sum(ofc$officer_killed == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   "Years" = yr_span(ofc_yr), "Version" = "2025")))
```

::: {.aa-downloads .cb-downloads}
{{< downloadthis data/derived/officer_shot_data_v2025.csv dname="officer_shot_data_v2025" label="Data (CSV)" >}}
{{< downloadthis data/derived/officer_shot_codebook_v2025.pdf dname="officer_shot_codebook_v2025" label="Codebook (PDF)" >}}
:::
:::

::: {.cb-reading}
::: {.cb-reason}
### One row per officer
`{r} nrow(ofc)` officers in `{r} length(unique(ofc$case_id))` incidents, `{r} ncol(ofc)` variables. Officers shot in the same incident share a `case_id`; incident-level columns repeat on each officer's row.
:::
::: {.cb-reason}
### Who counts as shot
An officer is included when struck by gunfire: wounds and grazes, rounds stopped by body armor or equipment, bullet fragments and ricochets, and fire from other officers (`blue_on_blue`). Injuries only from glass or debris are not counted. The codebook gives the full rules.
:::
::: {.cb-reason}
### Linked to the Active Attack Data
`aad_case_code` matches `case_code` in the Active Attack Data, so incident details (location, attacker, casualties) can be joined in. Officer details come from news and agency reports, prosecutor and court records, and FBI LEOKA.
:::
::: {.cb-reason}
### Reading the file
Read `officer_id` as text: officer 30.10 is not 30.1, and spreadsheet programs will merge them. Officers are named where their names were released; attackers are never named, and the notes say "the attacker" instead.
:::
:::
